extracted.intended_audience: People wanting to ask questions on Mathematics Stack Exchange (students at any level and professionals in related fields)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for what topics and question types are appropriate to ask on Mathematics Stack Exchange, and where alternative topics belong. Includes on-topic subjects, off-topic subjects, cross-site routing, and procedural advice (searching, self-answering, proposing sites).

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics Stack Exchange is for people studying mathematics at any level and professionals in related fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes who the site is intended for; tailor questions to be mathematical and suitable for learners or professionals rather than purely domain practitioners outside mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding mathematical concepts and theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: We welcome questions about understanding mathematical concepts and theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask clear conceptual questions seeking explanation, clarification, or insight into definitions, theorems, and their meaning or consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course/textbook-style mathematical problems
rubrics_metrics.description: We welcome mathematical problems such as one might come across in a course or textbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If asking a problem of this sort, first read the 'how to ask a good question' page; show your work and explain where you're stuck to improve chances of a helpful answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical puzzles
rubrics_metrics.description: We welcome questions about solving mathematical puzzles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Puzzle questions should be clearly mathematical in nature; provide sufficient statement and context so others can engage with the puzzle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software used by mathematicians (with exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: We welcome questions about software that mathematicians use (except Mathematica, which has its own Stack Exchange site).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software questions should be about tools commonly used in mathematical work; Mathematica-specific issues should be directed to the dedicated Mathematica site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-level mathematics should go to MathOverflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Research-level mathematics: MathOverflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the question is research-level (aimed at professional research mathematicians), consider posting on MathOverflow instead of Mathematics Stack Exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis questions (better on Cross Validated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical analysis: Cross Validated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions primarily about statistical methods, inference, or applied statistics are usually a better fit for Cross Validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-level algorithm design and complexity (better on Theoretical Computer Science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research level algorithm design, complexity theory, etc.: Theoretical Computer Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highly theoretical computer-science questions about algorithms and complexity that are research-level should be asked on Theoretical Computer Science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical analysis and scientific computing (better on Computational Science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical analysis and scientific computing: Computational Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions focused on numerical methods, high-performance scientific computing, and related implementation at scale belong on Computational Science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm implementation / computer simulation (better on Stack Overflow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithm implementation/design, computer simulation and modelling, etc.: Stack Overflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical programming/implementation problems, debugging code, or simulation-engine issues should be asked on Stack Overflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other computer science topics (better on Computer Science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other computer science topics: Computer Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General computer-science conceptual questions (not strictly mathematical) are likely a better fit for the Computer Science site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signal processing questions (better on Signal Processing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signal processing: Signal Processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions whose primary focus is signal processing techniques should be directed to the Signal Processing site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics education / pedagogy (better on Mathematics Educators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical education, especially about teaching and pedagogy: Mathematics Educators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about pedagogy, classroom practice, curriculum design, or teaching methods belong on Mathematics Educators.

rubrics_metrics.name: History and development of mathematics (better on History of Science and Mathematics)
rubrics_metrics.description: History and development of mathematics: History of Science and Mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical questions about the development of mathematical ideas or biography of mathematicians are better asked on the History of Science and Mathematics site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain-specific questions (physics, engineering, finance) are off-topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Physics, engineering and financial questions. It is fine to ask about the mathematical models and techniques, but concepts of the field would be off-topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the core of your question is a field-specific concept (e.g., physics theory or engineering practice), ask on the appropriate site (Physics, Electrical Engineering, Quantitative Science). Keep questions here focused on the mathematics rather than domain-specific interpretation or practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typesetting and TeX questions are off-topic here
rubrics_metrics.description: Typesetting equations — you can read our guideline for writing equations on this site, or visit the TeX - LaTeX Stack Exchange for questions about TeX and friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For formatting or TeX-specific help, follow the site's typesetting guideline or ask on the TeX - LaTeX site rather than asking general typesetting questions here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerology is off-topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about numerology are not appropriate for the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal advice about courses/careers is off-topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions seeking personal advice for choosing a course, academic program, career path, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such questions should be directed to those employed by the institution in question, or other qualified individuals who know your specific circumstances; they are not suitable for this Q&A format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions about the site belong on Mathematics Meta
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about the site itself should be asked on Mathematics Meta instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the community's Meta site for policy, moderation, or site-feature questions rather than asking them as regular Math.SE questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for duplicates before asking
rubrics_metrics.description: Please look around to see if your question has been asked before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searching existing questions reduces duplicates; if an existing question already answers your problem, use that instead. Links to searching tools and suggestions appear in the help center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-answering is allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: It's also OK to ask and answer your own question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you've solved a problem yourself and want to share the question and solution, you may post both; follow the normal quality guidelines when doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-site routing and proposing new sites
rubrics_metrics.description: If your question is not specifically on-topic for Mathematics Stack Exchange, it may be on topic for another Stack Exchange site. If no site currently exists that will accept your question, you may commit to or propose a new site at Area 51.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider other Stack Exchange communities for off-topic-but-valid questions; use Area 51 to propose new communities if necessary.
